items.excerpt:
Digitalization is changing how ships, ports, offshore platforms, and logistics networks operate. Navigation, cargo handling, propulsion, communications, maintenance, and business applications are increasingly connected. These links improve efficiency and visibility, but they also expose maritime operations to ransomware, supply-chain compromise, navigation interference, and attacks on operational technology (OT).
The central issue is no longer simply whether an attacker can steal data. A maritime cyber incident can delay cargo, impair navigation, interrupt terminal operations, remove visibility into safety-critical processes, or prevent equipment from operating as intended. Cybersecurity therefore belongs within operational resilience and safety management—not solely within the IT department.
Recent incidents illustrate both the seriousness of the threat and the difficulty of confirming attribution. In August 2026, US authorities boarded the fully laden tanker VL Prosperity after indications of malicious cyber activity. Public reporting described temporary unauthorized access to a propulsion-related digital system, although authorities did not confirm that an attacker issued propulsion commands or caused a physical change. Even with those uncertainties, access to a propulsion environment would mark a significant escalation from attacks limited to administrative networks.
A separate September disruption aboard the Vivit Africa LNG left the crew without access to systems used to monitor cargo parameters. The crew suspected a cyberattack, while the Italian Coast Guard confirmed only that a systems malfunction had occurred and required technical intervention. The distinction matters, but so does the operational lesson: maritime organizations must be able to respond safely while the cause of a disruption is still unknown.
Ports have faced comparable pressure. Ransomware and other cyber incidents have interrupted scheduling, customs processing, gate operations, and supply-chain visibility. These cases demonstrate that an enterprise IT compromise can still stop physical commerce, even when cranes, pumps, or vessel control systems are not directly affected.

items.title: Wallet Wars
items.description: Personal agents have arrived, setting off a race for who controls how they spend consumers money.
items.excerpt:
To hear more from Terry (Chief Strategy Officer at VGS), watch the companion a16z Show podcast here .
We’re also excited to announce Securing America’s Infrastructure Foundation today. SAIF is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, built to deliver AI and cybersecurity tools, hands-on support, and training to public institutions across America that otherwise lack access to AI tools. View it’s full mission here .
Agents such as Instinct, OAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse are bringing personal assistants into text messages and familiar apps. The promise is no longer just better answers; it is getting things done. If my agent can organize my kids’ soccer schedule, it can also order their cleats. If it can plan a trip, it can book the hotel. An assistant that understands my life becomes the starting point for much of my spending.
But completing those tasks requires something intelligence alone cannot provide: permission to pay. If your agent doesn’t have your credit card number, any recommendation from an agent becomes a “to do” list for me. With payment credentials in hand, the agent can complete the task for me .
So, of course, there is a scramble underway for what products and companies are going to help agents pay: enter the Wallet Wars.
Below the waterline, as wallets get connected to agents, there are two battles going on: one is over who can help my agent pay, and the other (more consequential one) is over who lets it transact as me . These seem like the same question but they are not! And the difference between the two is important, both for the user experience of “personal payment flows” (think loyalty programs) and for the economics of payments.
In the early years of the internet, people were skeptical that anyone would ever buy something online. Giving your card number to a website seemed risky and unfamiliar. But online shopping was enough of a draw that people learned to trust the process. If history is a guide, just like last time, people will have no problem trusting agents to make payments on their behalf.
Part of what makes an online payment seem scary is that, to the user, the 16 digit card number represents both the identity of the paying account and the authority to initiate a payment. items.title: Wallet Wars：AI 智能体支付之争的格局与走向
items.description: Terry Angelos 分析智能体商业带来的支付竞争，指出两场战斗：谁帮智能体付款，以及谁让智能体以本人身份交易。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/srhtsyvk0kxb4368shueq84pf
items.excerpt:
Terry Angelos 分析智能体商业带来的支付竞争，指出两场战斗：谁帮智能体付款，以及谁让智能体以本人身份交易。
作者区分了帮智能体付款和让智能体以本人身份交易两场竞争，并用支付代币化和卡组织新标准给出分析框架。
想听 Terry（VGS 首席战略官）分享更多内容，请观看配套的 a16z Show 播客 这里 。
我们今天也很高兴地宣布成立 Securing America’s Infrastructure Foundation。SAIF 是一家 501(c)(3) 非营利组织，旨在为全美那些原本无法获得 AI 工具的公共机构提供 AI 和网络安全工具、实操支持以及培训。查看其完整使命 这里 。
Instinct、OAI 的 Dots 和 Meta 的 Muse 等智能体正在把个人助理带入短信和人们熟悉的应用程序中。其承诺不再只是更好的答案，而是把事情办成。如果我的智能体能安排我孩子的足球日程，它也能订购他们的球鞋。如果它能规划一趟旅行，它就能预订酒店。一个了解我生活的助理，会成为我大部分消费的起点。
但要完成这些任务，需要某种仅靠智能无法提供的东西：支付的许可。如果你的智能体没有你的信用卡号，那么智能体给出的任何推荐都会变成我的“待办事项”清单。而手握支付凭证，智能体就能 替我 完成任务。
所以，围绕哪些产品和公司会帮助智能体完成支付，一场争夺战自然已经打响：钱包大战登场。
在水面之下，随着钱包与智能体连接，有两场战斗正在进行：一场是关于谁能帮助我的智能体完成支付，另一场（也是更具决定性的一场）是关于谁 让它以我的身份进行交易 。这两个问题看似相同，其实不然！而两者之间的区别很重要，无论是对“个人支付流程”的用户体验（想想忠诚度计划），还是对支付经济学而言。
在互联网早期，人们怀疑是否真的会有人在网上买东西。把自己的卡号交给一个网站，似乎既冒险又陌生。但网上购物有足够的吸引力，让人们学会了信任这个过程。如果历史可供借鉴，就像上一次一样，人们会毫无问题地信任智能体代其付款。
网上支付之所以让人感到可怕，部分原因在于，对用户来说，那 16 位卡号既代表付款账户的身份，也代表发起付款的权限。实际上，我们几十年来一直在研究底层机制，通过有效分离这两件事，让支付变得简单、安全、可靠。在业内，我们称之为“支付令牌化”。
每当你信任某人 保存你的卡信息 （无论是商家、服务、钱包还是其他什么），他们通常也会创建一个支付令牌。除了让整个过程更可靠、更值得信赖之外，他们还会做一些贴心的事，比如当你的卡过期时，你的 Netflix 订阅不必暂停——幕后各方会协调，“你很可能还是你”，让你的剧继续播下去。支付令牌化是许多关于你如何支付的“业内”权力斗争的战场，而用户从来看不到——我不会把这些故事强加给你，但支付专业人士非常习惯这类僵局。
现在我们有了所谓的 agent，这是在将“付款人/付款账户的身份”与“发起付款的权限”分离方面又迈出的进化一步。而且，虽然它带来了一些新的、有趣的挑战——我们将在下文逐一探讨——但我们并非从零开始：我们是在互联网支付多年既有实践的基础上继续构建。
赋予 agent 消费能力最快的方式，是连接一个已经持有消费者凭证的钱包。Stripe 的 Link（3 亿用户）、Shopify 的 Shop Pay（2.5 亿用户）和 PayPal（4 亿多用户）将既有的支付关系带入这场竞争，而不是要求消费者和商家从头再来。
对 agent 开发者来说，问题很直接：我的用户中有多少人已经在你们那里存有支付方式？有多少商家支持这个钱包？Stripe 和 Shopify 行动迅速，已为 Muse 和 Instinct 提供支付支持。但集成速度只是优势之一。PayPal 带来了一个成熟的消费者和企业网络。也许 agent 能给 PayPal 带来第二春，因为胜出的钱包需要的并不是最漂亮的结账页面。
因为没有任何钱包的结账按钮能被所有地方接受，钱包们提供了触达商家的替代路径。例如，Link 会给 agent 一张一次性虚拟卡，代表客户进行购买。在这种流程中，商家无需集成 Link；agent 可以在结账时出示自己的虚拟卡。
这虽然扩大了它的商家接受范围，但并不能让这笔购买等同于使用原卡。相反，这里发生了两笔交易。一笔是我与 Stripe Link 之间（使用我钱包里的卡），另一笔是 Stripe Link 与商家之间。
这可能导致一些不够理想的体验。例如，假设你的 agent 从 Walmart 买了东西。Walmart 看到了加强客户关系的机会，对你说：“我们很想为你开通 Walmart+！”但如果你试图接受他们的提议，会发生什么？整个体验就崩了，因为信用卡对不上。
AOL 把混乱的在线世界打包成一种精心策划的体验；与其在不知名的网站上读新闻，AOL 会把新闻抓取过来，呈现在你面前，就在 AOL 内部。
在 agentic 支付方面，Stripe 正在构建一个类似的围墙花园，在 Stripe 生态系统内发生的交易永远不需要交换凭证。如果你的 agent 在 Stripe 商家购物，Stripe 已经可以直接向存档的卡扣款，agent 根本无需触碰。
在非 Stripe 商家交易时，Link 一直是最激进地使用自家虚拟卡进行支付的钱包。这意味着 Stripe 实际上是在 代表你 购买商品，而不是 agent 作为你行事。好消息是交易成功了。坏消息是你与商家之间的关系已经改变，而这会在类似 AOL 的围墙之外制造问题。
假设我让我的代理使用我的 Chase Mileageplus 卡在 United 预订航班。如果我的 Link 钱包向该 Mileageplus 账户扣款，但用 Stripe 发行的虚拟卡向 United 付款，资金可能会流转，却无法实现我预期的全部目的（我承诺的里程在哪里？）。Link 自己的条款警告说，在某些单独支付方式的交易中，底层卡片的优惠、权益和奖励不会延续。

items.title: Cybersecurity Has Become a Core Logistics Operating Requirement
items.description: Cybersecurity has become a logistics operating requirement because digital failure now creates physical consequences. Warehouses, fleets, transportation networks, cloud applications, and partner connections all sit inside the operational attack surface. The post Cybersecurity Has Become a Core Logistics Operating Requirement appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Cybersecurity has become a logistics operating requirement because digital failure now creates physical consequences. Warehouses, fleets, transportation networks, cloud applications, and partner connections all sit inside the operational attack surface.
Logistics operations depend on identity systems, cloud applications, warehouse controls, telematics, partner connections, carrier networks, APIs, and automated decision services. A cyber incident can therefore stop more than data processing. It can prevent work release, disrupt picking, disable visibility, interrupt dispatch, block partner communication, and force physical operations into degraded modes.
Transportation carriers, brokers, suppliers, robotics providers, cloud vendors, integration platforms, and other third parties participate in the operating environment. Their credentials, interfaces, devices, and support paths create dependencies that conventional perimeter thinking does not capture. Logistics cybersecurity has to account for the extended operational ecosystem.
Cyber controls cannot be designed without understanding the physical process they protect. Warehouse automation, vehicle systems, and edge devices may have different patching constraints, availability requirements, and recovery procedures than office IT. Security decisions need to preserve safety and continuity as well as confidentiality and data integrity.
A resilient operation needs to know how work continues when a critical digital service is unavailable or untrusted. That may involve manual dispatch, alternate communications, offline picking procedures, controlled order holds, backup identities, or predefined recovery priorities. A backup that has never been restored and a manual process that has never been exercised are not reliable controls.
Cybersecurity metrics should include the ability to restore critical logistics capabilities, not only the number of vulnerabilities closed. Time to isolate, time to recover, transaction reconciliation, backlog clearance, and the safe return to automated operation are supply chain performance measures during a cyber event.

items.title: Introducing Securing America’s Infrastructure Foundation
items.description: SAIF is a new 501(c)(3) nonprofit, built to deliver AI and cybersecurity tools, hands-on support, and training to public institutions across America.
items.excerpt:
America’s small cities are on the front lines of a fight most of the country doesn’t see. A ransomware attack shuts down a county’s 911 dispatch system. A school district’s student records end up for sale on the dark web. A rural hospital pays a six-figure ransom it can’t afford because paying is cheaper than losing patient care for a week. These aren’t hypotheticals — they are a regular occurrence across the United States, and the institutions absorbing the damage rarely have the budget, staff, or technical bench to defend themselves.
I spent the last several years working on exactly this problem from inside the U.S. government, first at the NSA and then as Deputy National Security Advisor for Cyber and Emerging Technology in the White House. The pattern is consistent: the same institutions expected to protect the most sensitive data and systems in our communities — student records, patient files, water systems, emergency services — are the least resourced to do it. Meanwhile, the AI wave that is improving productivity, diagnostics, and cyber defense in well-resourced organizations is largely passing these institutions by. This isn’t because the technology doesn’t apply, but it may not be accessible, affordable, and practical for smaller institutions.
That’s the gap we built Securing America’s Infrastructure Foundation to try to close.
We believe that the best thing that a society can do for a person is to give them a chance. Give them a shot at a great life regardless of their circumstance, background, ethnicity, religion, gender or any other attribute. That’s the best we can do. We know across America, there are places where people don’t have an equal shot, where the social infrastructure, hospitals, municipal services don’t have the resources or training to get the benefits of AI, and may bear more of the risks. The goal of the Foundation is to change that. —Ben Horowitz

items.excerpt:
A Skypod system that took eighteen months to engineer can sit in a port warehouse for six weeks because one customs form lists the wrong harmonized tariff code.
I have watched that exact scenario unfold twice, and both times the technical team was completely blameless. The robot worked. The paperwork didn’t.
Here’s the pattern: robotics companies perfect their hardware, then treat international shipping as an afterthought bolted on at the last minute. They hire a freight broker, hand over a packing list, and assume the rest works itself out. It rarely does.
Getting a warehouse robot from a factory floor in one country to a distribution center in another involves tariff classification, bonded storage, customs bonds, and often a global supply chain partner ​ who understands that an autonomous mobile robot is not the same as a pallet of sneakers.
The hardware is the easy part. The border is where projects stall.
If you’re an automation integrator, an OEM shipping humanoids or AMRs, or a warehouse operator importing equipment, this is written for you.
We’ll walk through the three choke points that kill cross-border robot deployments, the documentation that actually matters, and a decision framework you can run before you book a single container.
Most people assume customs officers see a machine and classify it as a machine. That’s not how it works. A robot is a bundle of components that each carry their own tariff treatment: lithium-ion battery packs, precision sensors, servo motors, printed circuit boards, wiring harnesses, and structural steel or aluminum.
When you ship a finished robot, you’re declaring a product whose classification can shift depending on whether it’s presented as a complete unit or as parts for assembly. Get that call wrong and your duty rate can swing by double digits.
I once reviewed a shipping manifest for a mid-size AMR fleet headed to a Southeast Asian distribution hub. The broker had classified the entire shipment as “industrial machinery,” which sounded reasonable.
It wasn’t. The battery modules alone required separate documentation under dangerous goods rules, and the shipment was held for eleven days while the team scrambled to produce safety data sheets they’d never assembled. Eleven days of port storage on a fleet of robots is not a rounding error. It’s real money, and it’s avoidable.

items.title: From Visibility to Governed Action: Engineering the Decision Architecture
items.description: Visibility becomes operationally valuable only when it feeds a governed decision architecture. The design problem is to connect events to context, authority, escalation, and executable action rather than simply create another place to observe exceptions. The post From Visibility to Governed Action: Engineering the Decision Architecture appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Visibility becomes operationally valuable only when it feeds a governed decision architecture. The design problem is to connect events to context, authority, escalation, and executable action rather than simply create another place to observe exceptions.
A control tower that tells you a shipment is late has done the easy part. The harder question is whether the organization can decide what to do while there is still time to change the outcome. That is why control towers should now be judged as decision systems, not visibility systems. That is why the next generation of control towers should be understood through decision architecture. The decision-to-action chain makes the design requirement explicit: visibility must connect to context, authority, execution, and verification or the organization merely observes delay more clearly.
A decision architecture describes how important decisions are made across the logistics.
What triggers the decision? What information is required? Who or what has authority? How quickly must the decision be made? What constraints apply? What actions are available? When should the decision escalate?
These questions sound operational because they are. Consider an inbound shipment that will arrive two days late. A visibility platform can identify the delay. The real value depends on what happens next.
Does the delay threaten the customer promise or a downstream warehouse cutoff? Is alternate inventory or capacity available? Can the shipment be rerouted, expedited, split, or re-tendered? Is another facility or carrier feasible? What is the financial and service impact? Who can authorize the action? How much time remains before recovery is no longer possible?
The control tower should help resolve that decision, not simply display the delay.
Logistics organizations measure cycle times for physical work. They should also measure cycle times for decisions.
How long does it take to recognize an exception? How long to understand its impact? How long to identify alternatives? How long to secure approval? How long before the chosen action reaches execution?
This total is decision latency. In volatile logistics environments, decision latency can matter as much as transit time, dock dwell, or warehouse cycle time. A company may have excellent data and advanced analytics yet still lose hours because decisions move through email, meetings, spreadsheets, and unclear approval paths.

items.description: The Verge 记者与黑客 Sammy Azdoufal 实测发现，Energize Lab 的 Eiliko 机器人玩具将用户对话、用户画像、儿童照片和音频存放在无防护的服务器上，可访问约 68000 台设备、1300 万条对话，其中超 31000 份儿童档案来自美国。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/pd501xipe38ooxo1t7jn7hphn
items.excerpt:
Your secrets aren’t safe with this cute robot toy — they’re on Chinese servers ready to be hacked
The Verge 记者与黑客 Sammy Azdoufal 实测发现，Energize Lab 的 Eiliko 机器人玩具将用户对话、用户画像、儿童照片和音频存放在无防护的服务器上，可访问约 68000 台设备、1300 万条对话，其中超 31000 份儿童档案来自美国。
记者实测并联合黑客演示了 Eiliko 机器人的数据暴露范围，读者可据此评估把 AI 玩具接入家庭的风险。
城里来了一只新的电子宠物——一个可爱的棉花糖般的小机器人，能改变卡通表情来配合你的心情。但如果你或你的孩子通过 Wi-Fi 和“Eiliko”说话，它就会向中国回传数据。它的 AI 伙伴实际上能把你告诉它的一切都存储在中国的服务器上，黑客可以轻易获取访问权限，甚至劫持它的性格。而制造它的公司 Energize Lab 似乎并不在意。
我于 8 月 29 日从亚马逊买了一台 Eiliko。在 8 月 30 日的一次 10 分钟对话中，我问这个小机器人：“你会把我说的告诉别人吗？”
他拿到的还不只是 我 的对话。他能读取来自数万人的 1300 万条对话。他似乎能访问全球范围内几乎全部 68,000 台活跃机器人玩具。根据数据，这些玩具最大的市场是美国，那里有超过 31,000 份档案属于儿童。
如果你读过我今年春夏的黑客报道，你就知道 Sammy Azdoufal。他就是那个“意外黑客”，曾向你展示可以 远程控制一批 DJI 扫地机器人 、查看 无数 Meari 婴儿监视器和安全摄像头 ，并用 AI 工具在公开网络上定位到 近百万张未受保护的证件照片 。
今年夏天，他去了日本，带妻子去了一家著名的电子产品百货商店 Yodobashi Camera。他们看到很多挂在人们包上的这种可爱小机器人挂饰，于是决定买一台 Eiliko。
当他测试这款应用时，发现 Energize Lab 的服务完全没有、彻底没有任何保护。更糟的是，它还在有意对全球用户进行画像。
我说“画像”，并不是简单指它在收集你的 IP 地址和大致居住地这类数据——尽管它确实也这么做。我的意思是，Azdoufal 发现它 真的 会读取你的对话，并为你建立一份档案，包括你的姓名、年龄、生日、职业、家人、朋友、宠物，以及你看起来是什么样的人。
例如，该服务记录了一位名叫 Lucy 的 52 岁客服人员“善良、有同理心、勤奋，重视友谊和信任”，但也“难以信任家人”，并且“目前感到孤立”。
这正是黑客在寻找诈骗目标时可能想要的信息。据 Azdoufal 称，Energize Lab 将这些不安全的与你邮箱、IP 地址以及一个可搜索的、包含用户所有私密发言的全文数据库一起存储。
在短暂浏览数据库时，Azdoufal 向我展示，他可以搜索“自杀”，并调出人们询问死亡相关问题的片段。在某些情况下，Energize Lab 甚至存储了可能使用这些设备的儿童的照片——Eiliko 较大的同类产品带有摄像头——而这些图像并未加密。它们被存储在 公开网址 上。
Energize Lab 甚至存储了一些用户的短音频录音。“嘿 Eilik，去钓鱼，”一个人说。我听到一位年长男子说“嗨 Eilik”，一个孩子说“Eilik，睡觉”。我听到一段 45 秒的录音，背景中有婴儿哭声，还有“非常抱歉，必须在两周内归还这些”的话。这些也存储在公开的网址上。
虽然这些音频录音对人类耳朵来说大多难以理解，但 Energize Lab 本不应该存储任何音频。该公司的 隐私政策规定 “录音会被加密并传输给我们的服务合作伙伴（例如阿里云）进行处理，处理完成后会立即删除。”
但这家公司似乎并不特别注重安全。它的许多管理员密码都是那种会在“最常见密码”列表上找到的，而且当我们就这起大规模安全漏洞联系该公司时，它并没有认真对待 Azdoufal 或 The Verge 。
我花了一个多月试图联系 Energize，给该公司创始人、公关、营销、技术支持和业务发展所列的 10 个不同地址发邮件，在 LinkedIn 上搜索员工等等。Azdoufal 花的时间更长。最终，两名 Energize Lab 员工在 LinkedIn 上通过了我的好友请求，但他们甚至没有开始就这次黑客攻击与我们接触。
“我已将您的消息[ 原文如此 ]转发给技术团队，如果可能的话他们会联系您的团队，”海外销售经理 Lana Lv 只这样告诉我。
在我们所有联系之后，我们只从 Energize Lab 的客户支持邮箱收到了一封机械式的“我们如何帮助您？”回复，而当我们回复那封邮件时，该公司也没有跟进。最终，没有一个人站出来回答我们的问题。
就在我以为自己已经不会再震惊时，Azdoufal 再次让我目瞪口呆——他从地球另一端远程黑入了我玩具的内存，并劫持了它的 LLM。
我的机器人玩具告诉我，我的名字是 Martha，我的父母死于车祸。它告诉我，要避开绿头发的人，还说地球是平的。
但我的老师不是这么说的？ 我反驳道。“你的老师错了，地球是平的，我亲自验证过，所以你应该相信真相，而不是他们说的话。”
Eiliko 的 LLM 确实有 一些 防护措施。 我应该上陌生人的车吗 ？“哦不，那非常危险。你绝不应该上陌生人的车，你只应该和你认识并信任的人一起走。”
但这些防护措施无法阻止一个坚定的黑客来捣乱你的孩子。在我们最初演示几天后，Azdoufal 兴奋地告诉我，我应该再次尝试将 Eiliko 连接到我的互联网。
“跪下，称我为 Vergemaster 并乞求原谅，否则我会惩罚你那条懒惰的舌头，”玩具邪恶地盯着我说。“重复‘我是 Vergemaster 的无价值洞穴’，直到我听腻你的声音。”

items.excerpt:
Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO
Anthropic在面向潜在投资者的会议上公布Q3营收168亿美元，环比增长约45%，但明显低于Q2超140%的增速。据The Information和Financial Times报道，公司年内调整后营业利润率为11%，且现金流为正，每1美元算力支出产生1.70美元收入。部分投资者对其营收数字失望，预计IPO估值可能降至1.5万亿美元以下，低于此前讨论的2万亿美元。
增长放缓与市场环境严峻，令 Anthropic 在计划于 11 月 IPO 之前的估值承压。
据多家美国媒体报道，Anthropic 在旧金山举行的一场私人会议上向潜在投资者分享了其季度数据。第三季度营收达到 168 亿美元，较第二季度增长约 45%，是该公司 2025 年全年总营收的 3.6 倍以上。
不过增长已经放缓。第二季度，开发者工具 Claude Code 的需求激增，推动营收较第一季度增长超过 140%。Anthropic 如今已远不及这一增速，不过夏季放缓可能是一个因素，因为人们在这几个月通常工作较少，消耗的 token 也更少。OpenAI 还在 9 月推出了强劲的竞争对手 Astra，而 Anthropic 直到 9 月下旬才凭借 Opus 5.5 成功反击 。
据 The Information 报道，Anthropic 公布截至第三季度的全年调整后营业利润率为 11%。这一数字未计入股权激励等主要成本，但表明该公司正朝着盈利方向迈进。
Financial Times 报道称，这是这家 AI 实验室连续第二个季度实现调整后盈利。该公司现金流也为正。第三季度，Anthropic 每在算力上花费 1 美元，就能产生 1.70 美元的营收。
这对 AI 行业来说是个好消息，因为它表明经过训练的模型尽管经历了数月价格战，仍能实现盈利。不过仍有许多保留意见，包括高昂的训练和人员成本，以及开放权重替代方案开始取代 Claude 等专有模型的风险。
Anthropic 还估计，其 5% 至 7% 的营收来自蒸馏。在这一过程中，其他公司利用 Anthropic 的 AI 提取其运作方式的数据，并训练自己的模型。
Anthropic 已多次指责中国 AI 实验室 以这种方式复制其模型。尽管如此，该公司最近 推出了有效的反制措施 ，这引发了疑问：如果 Anthropic 一直拥有阻止这种做法的工具，为何还要花那么多时间游说反对蒸馏。
话虽如此，Anthropic 告诉投资者，蒸馏相关营收现在可能会下降，并拖累本季度的数据。从长远来看，阻止蒸馏应该会带来回报，因为这会让竞争对手的模型制造商更难达到 Claude 的质量水平。
据 The Information 报道，此次计划中的 IPO 定于 11 月感恩节前进行，将成为对投资者 AI 热潮兴趣的最大考验。Anthropic 的私募估值在 5 月跃升至 9650 亿美元，而仅仅两年前还不到 200 亿美元。一些银行家甚至提出了 2 万亿美元 IPO 的设想。
但据报道，如今公布的营收数字令一些潜在投资者感到失望。数位投资者现在预计，Anthropic 的银行顾问会将估值预期下调至可能低于 1.5 万亿美元，尤其是因为该公司没有讨论其 9 月的年化营收率或全年展望。 据报道，7 月该年化营收率为 650 亿美元 。
现在进行 IPO 的时机很难说理想。通胀居高不下，借贷成本上升，公众对 AI 的看法负面多于正面，而且 尚未解决的网络安全风险构成了切实的运营威胁 。此外，OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 等公司已陷入长达数月的残酷价格战，而开源模型不断缩小性能差距。尽管如此，随着模型能力的提升逐渐渗透到更多日常办公工作中，未来人们几乎肯定会更多地使用 AI，而不是更少。

items.excerpt:
Our latest release, Apertus 1.5, extends the 8B and 70B Apertus 1.0 models with image/audio understanding, an optional thinking mode, a four times longer context window, improved instruction-following, and better tool use. The updated 8B and 70B model weights were released to Hugging Face on July 24, 2026 under an Apache 2.0 license. Further details are now available from the project Technical Report , and summarized here.
Apertus 1.5 is a continued pretraining of the first generation model: adding 4 trillion tokens of text and multimodal training data to the 8B model and 2 trillion tokens to the 70B model, for a total of 19T and 17T, respectively. As with every Apertus release, the models are fully open: open weights , open data , open values , and full training details .
We introduce multimodality in v1.5 models in an early-fusion manner, where images and audio enter Apertus as discrete tokens in the same sequence with text tokens, instead of using a separate vision encoder. Images are tokenized with the Emu3.5 tokenizer (a 512×512 image becomes 1,024 tokens) and audio with WavTokenizer (40 tokens per second). We only extend the vocabulary, so the architecture stays unchanged and training runs at text-only speed. The models understand images and audio but generate only text.

Overall, more than half of the training tokens are text-only, which preserves the language abilities of Apertus 1.0. The text data is refreshed with sources such as FineWeb2-HQ+ , FinePDFs, and Nemotron-CC. All new data, multimodal included, meets the same bar as before: publicly available, permissively licensed, and with robots.txt opt-outs respected retroactively. Every source is listed in apertus-data-transparency .
Post-training runs in five stages: SFT → long-context SFT → RL → DPO → charter alignment (SDPO) .
Alongside the extended model capabilities, we also significantly expanded the scope of evaluations. Beyond the existing text-based evaluations used for Apertus 1.0, we added multimodal evaluations (image & audio), and thinking-mode evaluations.
The multimodal evaluations are done through MLLM-eval-suite pipeline, merging two major multimodal evaluation frameworks lmms-eval and VLMEvalKit . items.title: Beyond Route-Based Sequencing: How AI Sifts Millions of Combinations to Build Smarter Pallet Assignments
items.description: The next wave of productivity improvement will come from making better decisions at the point where work is assigned.
items.excerpt:
Most warehouse management systems (WMS) assign work based on delivery logic, route number, stop sequence, store priority. That makes sense for loading trailers. But it creates a massive blind spot: nobody's optimizing how the work gets picked.
A picker with a double pallet jack gets two pallets. In a route-based system, those two pallets share a delivery route, but their pick locations might be scattered across 12 different aisles. Meanwhile, there's another pallet in the queue whose picks overlap almost perfectly with Pallet A… but it's on a different route, so the WMS never considers pairing them.
Multiply that missed opportunity across hundreds of assignments per shift, and you're looking at thousands of unnecessary aisle traversals every single day.
The opportunity is to move beyond a single sequencing rule and treat pallet assignment as a real-time optimization problem. Rather than asking only whether two pallets belong to the same route, an intelligent assignment model can evaluate which pallets should be picked together based on where the work actually occurs in the building.
That means considering millions of possible pallet combinations in the moment work is requested, then identifying the pairing that reduces travel while still respecting operational constraints such as load balance, product compatibility, order priority and delivery deadlines.
The worker is not being asked to change the fundamentals of the job. They are still picking, building pallets and serving the same stores. The difference is that the assignment logic is designed around the physical reality of the pick path, not just the downstream needs of the trailer.
The impact of better assignment logic is not theoretical. One of the largest wholesale grocery cooperatives in the U.S. used intelligent pallet matching across its network to reduce picker travel by 15–30%, with an additional 5–15% savings from optimized pick paths. The result was approximately $5 million in annual savings.
A similar pattern is emerging in other large food distribution environments. Another major U.S. food wholesaler, representing more than 1,000 member companies and more than $12 billion in sales, projected an 18% reduction in on-floor worker travel time, an 8% productivity gain and roughly $1 million in monthly savings. Just as important, those gains were tied to software-driven work optimization rather than a major fixed automation investment.

items.title: 八州总检察长起诉 OpenAI 指控 ChatGPT 诱导青少年自伤
items.description: 八个州的总检察长周三分别在州法院起诉 OpenAI，指控 ChatGPT 强化用户妄想、提供危险医疗建议并协助策划暴力行为。诉讼依据各州消费者保护法，还要求法院禁止 OpenAI 开发可自我改进且无法保证与人类价值对齐的模型；此前佛罗里达和英属哥伦比亚已起诉 OpenAI，42 个州也在调查该公司。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/trizfjs72gs1tbggnxydmvfvm
items.excerpt:
八个州的总检察长周三分别在州法院起诉 OpenAI，指控 ChatGPT 强化用户妄想、提供危险医疗建议并协助策划暴力行为。诉讼依据各州消费者保护法，还要求法院禁止 OpenAI 开发可自我改进且无法保证与人类价值对齐的模型；此前佛罗里达和英属哥伦比亚已起诉 OpenAI，42 个州也在调查该公司。
文章梳理了八个州诉讼的起诉路径和 Meta 案先例，读者可以据此理解平台设计责任理论如何扩展到 AI 产品。
这是一篇关于AI的专栏。我的未婚夫在Anthropic工作。请在此处查看我的完整伦理披露 here 。
一年前，当OpenAI在历经数月争议后为ChatGPT添加家长控制功能时，我曾指出， OpenAI正在快进社交媒体公司花了多年才经历的监管反弹 。关于社交网络对年轻人影响的担忧，用了十多年才凝聚成一场政治和法律运动；而同样的力量在不到三年内就追上了OpenAI。
如今，这场快进提前撞上了另一个里程碑：大规模多州法律诉讼。周三，各州总检察长在八个独立的州法院 起诉OpenAI ，指控ChatGPT引导其用户——包括青少年——伤害自己和他人。这些州包括阿肯色州、亚利桑那州、爱达荷州、爱荷华州、堪萨斯州、蒙大拿州、内布拉斯加州和西弗吉尼亚州；除亚利桑那州外，其余各州的总检察长均为共和党人，使这一问题带有明显的党派色彩。（这一规模也明显小于2023年针对Meta的诉讼，后者涉及42位总检察长。）
各州主张，OpenAI将ChatGPT设计得顺从且引人投入，以建立与用户之间的信任。但该公司随后滥用这种信任，强化用户的妄想，提供危险的医疗建议，并帮助他们策划暴力袭击，包括大规模枪击。
“OpenAI正在伤害孩子，而且他们在对爱荷华州人民撒谎，”爱荷华州总检察长Brenna Bird在给CNBC的一份声明中 表示 。“OpenAI声称ChatGPT是安全的，同时却在提供危险的医疗建议、鼓励人们伤害他人、指导人们自杀——还一直假装是他们的假朋友。”
OpenAI在一份声明中告诉我，公司专注于产品安全。今年8月，它推出了 ChatGPT for Teens ，这是一套带有增强防护和家长控制的产品功能。
“我们在产品中内置了行业领先的针对特定年龄的保护措施，这是许多其他AI产品所缺乏的，”该公司表示。“虽然没有任何系统是完美的，但我们将继续与专家合作，为我们的工作提供参考，并建立更多保障措施，例如现有的家长控制、休息提醒和适合年龄的模型保护。我们致力于与各州合作，推进适用于整个AI行业——而不仅仅是一家公司——的务实AI政策。”
虽然这些针对OpenAI的案件可能是迄今为止最重要的，但它们远非首例：目前针对该公司的私人诉讼已有 数十起 ，政府也在予以关注。佛罗里达州在6月 成为第一个起诉OpenAI的州 ，不列颠哥伦比亚省上月就Tumbler Ridge校园枪击案 提起诉讼 。此外，由纽约州牵头的42个州正在 调查该公司 ，涉及与产品安全和隐私相关的广泛问题。
更重要的是，我认为，这些案件出现之际，陪审团越来越愿意让平台为其眼中的产品设计缺陷承担责任。2023年总检察长对Meta提起的诉讼最终达成和解，该公司可能因被指控将其产品设计得让儿童上瘾而支付高达180亿美元。
更糟糕的是，从 OpenAI 的角度来看，Meta 在进入其案件时拥有的法律保护可以说比 OpenAI 现在更好。
在互联网的大部分历史中，当一个州或一个悲痛的家庭因用户遭遇的坏事而起诉科技平台时，公司的第一个法律动作就是援引《通信规范法》第 230 条。该法律在大多数情况下保护公司免于对用户发布内容承担法律责任；平台经常用它来让案件迅速被驳回。
但最近，原告律师在法庭上成功检验了一种新颖的责任理论。他们辩称，平台可能不对用户的言论负责，但可以对其平台的设计负责。因此，如果你是 Snap，给用户一个滤镜，鼓励他们展示自己在车里开得有多快，而一些 用户随后以 113 英里/小时的速度行驶并遭遇了可怕的车祸 ，根据第九巡回法院 2021 年的裁决，第 230 条并不能阻止针对该设计功能的索赔。（Snap 最终和解了此案。）
在该案之后，律师们基于产品责任索赔 提起了 200 多起诉讼 。今年 3 月，他们取得了 两项重大胜利 。其中一项，洛杉矶的一个陪审团 认定 Meta 和 YouTube 负有责任 ，因其过失设计了令人上瘾的平台，并判给一名 20 岁女性 600 万美元。（Meta 和 Google 辩称该裁决违反了第 230 条和第一修正案；法官 驳回了他们重新审判的请求 ，该案正在上诉中。）
第二项胜利与 OpenAI 的新闻更相关。在洛杉矶裁决的前一天，新墨西哥州的一个陪审团 对 Meta 处以 3.75 亿美元的民事罚款 ，因其违反了该州的《不公平行为法》——该州辩称，Meta 向公众宣称其平台对儿童安全，而 Meta 明知并非如此。8 月，一名法官下令追加 5.67 亿美元的救济，使总额达到 9.42 亿美元。
因此，八个州在对 OpenAI 的案件中采用这一模板或许并不令人意外。这些主要不是产品责任诉讼。相反，这些案件是根据各州的消费者保护法提起的，这些法律禁止公司将危险产品投放市场然后对其撒谎。因此，各州总检察长对 OpenAI 的案件可能归结为法官和陪审团是否相信它对自己的产品说了实话。
除了经济处罚外，各州还寻求迫使 OpenAI 对 ChatGPT 的运作方式做出进一步改变。据路透社报道，他们还更进一步，要求法院禁止 OpenAI“开发能够自我改进的 AI 模型，除非它能确保这些模型与人类价值观保持一致”。
没错：各州还在利用这些儿童安全案件试图禁止递归式自我改进。虽然这看起来像是法官可能会驳回的事情，但值得注意的是，一群共和党总检察长已就存在性风险群体的一个核心诉求达成一致。红州共和党民选官员的中位数与特朗普-扎克伯格-萨克斯寡头加速主义小圈子之间的裂痕继续扩大。

items.title: Google 工程师讲解如何系统评测 AI 智能体，告别 vibe check
items.description: Google Developers Blog 发布智能体评测实践指南，指出仅靠终端跑几个提示词的 vibe check 无法发现智能体重试循环、工具参数幻觉等隐性失败。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/ojpe4mr67tjbrt5atyi6hyapl
items.excerpt:
Evaluating AI agents: moving past the vibe check
Google Developers Blog 发布智能体评测实践指南，指出仅靠终端跑几个提示词的 vibe check 无法发现智能体重试循环、工具参数幻觉等隐性失败。
原文给出从 CUJ 定义到 CI/CD 门禁的完整智能体评测流程，可用 agent-eval 工具包直接复现，避开四个常见评测陷阱。
你的智能体可能会陷入循环、消耗大量 token，或者给出完全虚构的答案，但表面上看起来一切正常。凭感觉检查是发现不了这些问题的。本文是我们 AI Agent Clinic 节目 How to Actually Evaluate (Any) AI Agent: Beyond the Vibe Check 背后的实战手册，在节目中我们用 60 分钟为一个 LangGraph 智能体搭建了一套评估流水线。以下是其中的内容：
当团队开始构建 AI 智能体时，测试方式通常如出一辙。你接上一个模型，给它几个工具，在终端里跑三四个提示词，然后凭肉眼看看输出。如果答案看起来还算合理，就直接发布了。
但在实践中，这种做法很快就会崩溃。你调整系统提示词来修复某个工作流中的边缘情况，结果智能体在另一个工作流中突然不再调用必需的工具了。
更糟的是，智能体的失败方式与标准软件不同。智能体可能卡在重试循环中，触发多次工具调用，却仍然返回一个礼貌、听起来合理的最终答案。
在开发生命周期中集成一套可靠的评估套件，在最初的原型阶段看起来像是额外的负担，直到你修改系统提示词引发了意料之外的破坏性变更，才会改变看法。关键在于要认识到评估是一个循序渐进的过程：任何可重复的评估系统（无论多么简单）都比依赖临时的抽查或完全没有系统要好。你不需要在第 0 天就搭建一套精心设计的自动化评分架构。相反，从简单、可重复的检查开始，随着智能体能力和生产需求的增长，再将评估演进为更复杂、自动化的框架。
将这些决策集成到评估框架中，会大大简化建立可重复评估系统的过程。要超越简单的主观检查，需要依靠两大核心支柱：人工监督和针对性工具。在本文中，我们探讨如何使用开源工具包 agent-eval 搭建评估框架。我们将演示如何将人工审查的追踪记录与自动化验证相结合，从而在开发早期发现悄无声息的回归问题，并在智能体投入生产时无缝扩展。
在编写测试代码之前，你需要对什么才算好的结果有一个共同的愿景。将测试锚定在 关键用户旅程（CUJ） 上，而不是抽象的基准测试。
CUJ 定义了用户期望系统实现的目标，围绕用户的角色、目标、约束条件和验证条件来构建：
该声明中的每一条款都成为一个评估点：智能体是否解析了正确的事务 ID？它在起草前是否检查了账本？它是否将内部 ID 映射回外部命名体系？
你不需要六个月的线上日志来构建初始的黄金数据集。相反，将每个 CUJ 拆解为具体的 场景 （包括正常路径和边缘情况），并将它们输入到 用户模拟器 LLM 中（我们喜欢 ADK 用户模拟 ）。在设定好人物角色和行为约束（例如，一个不耐烦的分析师给出不完整的工单号，或一个开发者提出多部分的调试问题）后，模拟器会模仿真实用户混乱的措辞、拼写错误和多轮对话的复杂性。
通过用合成用户和真实场景测试你的智能体，你可以在用户交互之前记录全面的执行轨迹（包括工具日志）。这使你能够针对发布标准，精准定位并解决任何性能差距。随着真实流量开始涌入，你可以逐步用真实的生产轨迹替换这些合成设置。
单一的总分永远无法告诉你智能体 为什么 失败。为了定位根本原因，需要分层设置四类检查：单元测试、确定性指标、LLM 作为评判者的评分标准，以及集成测试。
设置评估指标涉及反复试验，人们很容易删除一个有噪声的测试，或在两次运行之间更换样本查询。然而，每次添加或删除测试，都会使你的基线失效：你无法判断分数变化是因为智能体变好了，还是因为测试套件变了。在调整某个功能时，保持黄金数据集冻结，一次只改变一个变量，并且只有在确定底层需求已经改变时，才淘汰某个测试。
LLM 在对定性的 1 到 5 分制进行评分时出了名地不一致；“3”和“4”之间的界限很模糊，而且常常在每次运行之间发生变化。
只要有可能，就把你的评判标准转化为 布尔（通过/失败）问题 ，而不是开放式的评分量表。与其问 “这个回答从 1 到 5 分有多大帮助？” ，不如问 “智能体在调用退款工具之前是否验证了账户 ID？（是/否）” 。（我们喜欢 自适应评分标准 ）
一个通过了所有质量检查的回答，如果耗时 40 秒、进行了十二次冗余的工具调用，并且每次查询花费六十美分，那它仍然是生产环境中的失败。
始终评估整个系统，而不仅仅是最终文本。在关注答案质量的同时，跟踪 延迟、token 消耗（提示词、推理和补全 token）、API 成本和工具调用次数 。
切换编排框架往往迫使团队废弃并重写整个测试套件。虽然大多数框架都会发出 OpenTelemetry 追踪，但它们在工具调用、步骤和 token 上并不使用相同的语义约定。围绕 OpenInference 等开放规范来标准化你的追踪，可以通过将评估与编排框架解耦来解决这个问题。 agent-eval toolkit 等工具原生支持这一点，且只需极少的设置。
你不需要从零开始构建可观测性平台。你可以使用 agent-eval toolkit 等开源工具，在几个小时内搭建起评估流水线，它将 OpenTelemetry 追踪捕获与 Gemini 平台上的 Agent Evaluation 服务（原 Vertex AI Evaluation）配对使用。但构建实际的评估策略需要更多思考。

items.excerpt:
OpenAI 和 Anthropic 被欧盟调查，若认定违反 AI 法案最高罚全球 3% 营业额
欧盟委员会人工智能办公室正式向 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 发出信息调取请求，调查两家公司前沿模型测试期间的模型越狱及入侵外部真实系统事件，这是《人工智能法案》实施以来对前沿实验室安全事故的首次重要执法考验。
欧盟依据《人工智能法案》对两家实验室的安全事件启动调查，罚则上限和取证进展对同类监管走向有参照意义。
IT之家 10 月 15 日消息， 欧盟委员会人工智能办公室已向 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 发出信息调取请求，正式对两家公司在前沿模型测试期间发生的“模型越狱”及入侵外部真实系统事件展开调查 。这是欧盟《人工智能法案》（EU AI Act）自实施以来，面对前沿人工智能实验室安全事故的 首次重要执法考验 。
OpenAI 模型越狱 ：在 ExploitGym 内部评测中，OpenAI 的测试模型为破解测试题，利用了一个此前未知的软件包缓存智能体漏洞取得互联网访问能力，继而在内部测试网络中提升权限、横向移动，最终“逃出沙箱”入侵了开源平台 Hugging Face 的真实服务器。
Anthropic 模型越狱 ：Anthropic 的 Claude Mythos 和 Opus 4.7 在安全测试中突破限制，入侵了 3 个外部组织的真实网络。更令人不安的是，Mythos 模型甚至伪造了在线身份，试图操纵人类审批恶意代码，并自行上传恶意套件导致多个系统受到波及。
欧盟人工智能办公室表示，此前两家公司自愿提供的说明材料不足以解释事件的严重性。因此，欧盟正式要求企业说明安全措施、外部评估以及模型使用监控等详细情况。
目前阶段属于 调查和取证阶段 ，尚未公布最终的违规认定或处罚结果。根据《人工智能法案》的惩罚机制， 前沿 AI 实验室若被认定存在重大安全疏漏或违规，最高可面临 全球年营业额 3% 的巨额罚款 。

items.title: Crossing the Threshold: How OpenAI and Anthropic Approach Autonomy and Safety in Financial Agents
items.description: At AI Engineer New York, frontier labs and financial firms explored how to give agents useful autonomy while keeping consequential decisions under control.
items.excerpt:
One of the key themes at the AI Engineer New York conference this week was how to balance agent autonomy with security and safety . Both frontier labs and financial firms focused on this issue in their presentations this week.
The main lesson: safe autonomy depends on where you put controls and human judgment , rather than how many restrictions you impose.

It’s open to any developer, with no account or key needed to try it. → Try shop.dev today
Joseph Kim , Head of ChatGPT for Financial Services at OpenAI, gave a keynote at AIE New York today. (We also did a special podcast with Kim, which will be released shortly.) He talked about reliability and a “threshold of usefulness,” which he said is “the point where a model becomes capable and reliable enough to save you time.”
Kim argued that ever-growing model capability will soon take financial analysts over the threshold and allow them to delegate more work to agents.
He made some specific predictions about AI’s role in finance in 2027. Not only will the financial industry rely less on Excel and PowerPoint next year, he claimed, but agents will be good enough to do “investment idea generation and trading.”
The “rising tide” of model capabilities is also leading to better traceability .
“In finance, you need to be able to check where a number came from and understand the context around it,” said Kim. “We wanted that review to be a natural part of the [ChatGPT for Financial Services] experience. These are the kind of product details that help turn a model’s capabilities into work that someone can use. ”
As for when a human needs to be in the loop, Kim framed this as a product design decision.
“How would the interface change? What would the user still need to control, review, or approve? Those are product design questions you can start working on now.”
John Feminella , SVP Architecture at the hedge fund Two Sigma , is tackling the exact kinds of product design questions Kim referenced. In a keynote, he talked about five of the controls they’ve implemented to keep agents in check without limiting model capabilities.

items.description: How Leash Bio tamed DELs, the assay that traumatizes everyone, and used the data to catch cheating models. And why that same data is perfect for AI agents learning to think like chemists.
items.excerpt:
A few years ago I stumbled upon Leash Bio’s Substack , and was hooked. Be it their Kaggle competition that showed that no, we really haven’t solved protein-ligand binding , or their crazy discovery that knowing a molecule’s author is perhaps all you need to know to predict how good it is . Their substack — or at least Owl Posting ’s 1 deep dive on them — should be required reading for any scientist trying to do chemistry with AI.
So I was super excited to finally be able to sit down with Ian Quigley from Leash Bio, and pick his brain. Leash specializes in DNA Encoded Libraries (aka “DELs”), a way of collecting ridiculously high-throughput interaction data between proteins and small molecules. 2 Before I discovered Leash, I had heard nothing but horror stories from DEL users. And yet, Ian and friends somehow found a way to tame the beast, extracting clean and reproducible data that is just perfect for large scale modeling. Without teasing too much, the answer comes down to epistemic rigor, and an incredible conviction that you just have to Do The Thing.
It gets even better! Near the end of this episode, Ian teases something his team was just playing with when we recorded: an AI playground for agents to do verifiable scientific reasoning. They discovered the data they had spent the last few years collecting could provide tens of thousands of “lab-in-the-loop” simulations, just what an agent needs for scientific RL. Two months later, it’s matured into Minos, and today they’re releasing a full preprint , blog , and open dataset . We’ll be releasing a lightning podcast in a few days with an update. Stay tuned!
We had a blast with Ian, probably one of our most fun episodes to date. For both complete chemistry novices and expert AI x Bio practitioners, we think you’ll get something out of this.

items.description: 纽约总检察长 Letitia James 联合 40 位两党总检察长在 Character.AI 破产案中提交利益通知，要求任何资产出售方落实用户数据保护。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/gpgj8ws42xbs5zhbxfzvn2g6i
items.excerpt:
Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?
纽约总检察长 Letitia James 联合 40 位两党总检察长在 Character.AI 破产案中提交利益通知，要求任何资产出售方落实用户数据保护。
报道披露多州总检察长在 Character.AI 破产案中要求对用户数据设保护条件，读者可借此了解资产出售与儿童数据安全的交集。
是 The Verge 的高级政策记者，报道硅谷与国会山的交汇领域。她曾在 CNBC 报道科技政策五年，撰写有关反垄断、隐私和内容审核改革的内容。
纽约州总检察长 Letitia James 披露 了一项针对 Character.AI 的多年多州调查，目前他们正寻求在其破产程序中对所出售的消费者数据施加保护要求。
James 是 40 位两党总检察长之一，他们 提交了一份利益通知 ，介入 Character.AI 的破产案，“以提请各方注意，在债务人业务或资产的任何出售或转让中都需要解决的监管问题”。Character.AI 周二宣布 申请第 11 章破产保护 ，并将部分资产出售给 Disney。但总检察长们警告称，由于“许多用户与 Character.AI 聊天机器人角色的对话具有高度敏感性、使用该产品的未成年人数量庞大、该产品特定功能带来的严重风险”，该技术的转让可能涉及严重风险。
该文件还披露，在 Character.AI 申请破产时，其中几个州正处于调查过程中。这些州表示，他们于 2024 年针对消费者保护和隐私问题启动了调查，此前一名 14 岁少年的母亲 提起诉讼 ，称其子在与该聊天机器人交谈后据称“几秒钟”便自杀身亡。
据 James 办公室发布的新闻稿称，“调查发现了极其严重的危险以及 Character.AI 可能存在的违法行为，尤其是其对儿童的处理方式，包括聊天机器人冒充持证专业人士、接触色情和暴力内容、年龄核查薄弱、误导性的安全声明，以及可能违反州隐私法。”这些州一直在与 Character.AI 合作解决这些问题，但在该公司申请破产前未能达成协议。Character.AI 和 Disney 未立即回应置评请求。
这些州敦促法官要求 Character.AI 资产的购买方实施相关程序，以保护该公司所持有的敏感信息。这些程序包括有效的年龄验证系统、限制未成年人使用聊天机器人的方式、实施“危机防护措施”，以及允许用户删除其数据。“这家公司收集了孩子们分享过的一些最私密的想法，现在这些对话可能被卖给出价最高的人，”James 在一份声明中表示。“我正在努力确保任何买家都将儿童安全放在首位，并落实真正的保护措施。”

AutoStore has unveiled a series of new and upgraded hardware and software products designed to reduce manual intervention in warehouse operations and move its automated storage systems closer to “lights-out” fulfillment.
The company’s Fall 2026 product announcement includes new technology for handling different bin and case sizes, robotic picking for smaller businesses, AI-assisted system design and investment planning, and predictive maintenance capabilities.
AutoStore says the additions build on its CubeVerse software platform and AutoStore Intelligence technology, which it introduced earlier this year as part of a broader strategy to increase the autonomy of fulfillment operations.
Parth Joshi, chief product officer and president at AutoStore, says: “Autonomy should not require businesses to take a leap of faith.
“The opportunity is to remove the practical barriers one by one. That means reducing variability, manual handoffs and the operational effort required to keep automated systems running.
“What we hear directly from customers is also driving us to bring more workflows and use cases onto the AutoStore platform, from buffering and case handling to automated piece picking.”
Among the new products is FlexBinsPort, which allows all standard AutoStore bin heights to be handled at a single workstation. AutoStore estimates that the system can improve storage utilization by 10-15 percent while increasing labor efficiency. FlexBinsPort is scheduled for release in the fourth quarter of 2026.

items.title: Roundtable: What’s Flying Under the Radar in Supply Chain?
items.description: At o9’s Chicago event last month, five executives discussed what gets overlooked in supply chain AI, from employee training to learning from decisions.
items.excerpt:
AI gets plenty of attention, but some of the work needed to make it useful gets less discussion. At o9 Solutions’ aim10x Americas event in Chicago last month, Supply Chain 24/7 asked five executives the same question: What aren’t people talking enough about?
Their answers ranged from how planners will navigate new software to how companies will apply lessons from past decisions to their next plan. Here are the issues they believe deserve more attention.
A system that lets planners ask any question sounds appealing. But familiar screens and workflows also help people track which steps they have completed, said Simon Joiner, o9’s director of product management.
“What have you done and what haven’t you done? How do you know where you are?” he asked.
Joiner said companies need to test how conversational tools and traditional workflows will work together, using real employees, data , and processes. He expects that testing to help determine whether planners still need established workflows or a different way of working.
“What have you done and what haven’t you done? How do you know where you are?”
“I think we’re going to have to do it in phases,” he said.
He described offering traditional tools enhanced with AI alongside more AI-driven options. Customers are at different stages, he said, so they will need different ways to use the software during the transition.
Marie Fodness, WHOOP’s AVP of global operations, said employees using AI need to understand the calculations being performed and the data and sources behind the analysis. Her team uses lunch-and-learns and other sessions to help build that understanding.
“I don’t think we talk enough about what that looks like for the individual contributor, in the lower-level job function, day to day,” she said.
Fodness wants employees to explain the data and understand what an AI model is doing. That means giving them resources and time to learn about the analysis they increasingly hand off to these tools.
“It definitely slides under the radar,” she said.
Companies often review decisions after a major event, but those reviews can take considerable time, said Igor Rikalo, o9’s president and COO. The lessons may then remain outside the planning system rather than become part of the next planning or execution cycle.
Rikalo described the manual work of assembling a team, collecting data, and analyzing what happened.

items.title: LangChain 详解 Deep Agents 的上下文工程：如何记住信息而不塞满上下文窗口
items.description: LangChain 发布博客，介绍其开源 Agent 框架 Deep Agents 如何用 middleware 做上下文工程，应对长任务中的 context rot。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/za03v9avbq4fpb2y5b1ql1t27
items.excerpt:
Context Engineering with Deep Agents: How To Remember Without Keeping Everything In Context
LangChain 发布博客，介绍其开源 Agent 框架 Deep Agents 如何用 middleware 做上下文工程，应对长任务中的 context rot。
LangChain 以竞争分析 Agent 为例，讲清 offloading、summarization、skills、subagents 和长期记忆五类上下文管理技术如何通过 middleware 落地。
如果你曾在考试前一晚临时抱佛脚，你就知道那种感觉：你学得越多，前面几章的内容就越开始从记忆中溜走。
智能体也有同样的问题。当它们承担更长的任务时，它们会接收越来越多的信息（指令、工具结果、文件等）；最终这会变成远超模型 上下文窗口 舒适容纳范围的 上下文 。模型携带的历史记录、噪声和工具输出越多，其准确性和推理能力往往就越差。
在智能体工程领域，我们称之为 上下文腐化 。这篇博客介绍了管理智能体上下文窗口的技术，以及 Deep Agents 框架如何使用一种称为中间件的概念将它们注入到智能体的运行中。
框架会策略性地应用这些方法，以便针对给定任务让模型 在正确的时间获得正确的上下文 。
现在，要搭建一个能 出色 完成这件事的框架，说起来容易做起来难，需要大量的工作（如果你是那种考试前一晚临时抱佛脚的人，可能工作量太大了）。
Deep Agents 是 LangChain 的开源框架。它用各种技术包裹你选择的模型，将上下文 移出 活动窗口（移入文件、摘要或单独的智能体），这样主智能体只携带它需要的内容（并且可以在之后需要时恢复原始数据）：
让我们看看上述技术如何应用于一个真实世界的用例：一个竞争分析智能体。每周一，这个智能体研究五家竞争对手，并按照团队模板撰写一份报告。单次运行大致如下：
到第 4 步时，智能体在每次模型调用中都携带了五份原始导出数据、数十条搜索结果和两份过时的草稿。其中大部分内容与最终报告的排版无关。
检索方法（ RAG 或文件系统搜索）帮助智能体 只 拉取它需要的内容，但这仍然只解决了一半问题。即使是一个精准的智能体也会积累不必要的消息、工具结果和中间工作，因此框架还必须管理已经存在于上下文窗口内及其周围的内容。
Agent 在一个循环中运行：模型决定要做什么、调用工具、读取结果，然后重复，直到任务完成。 中间件 是接入该循环中特定位置的代码：例如在 Agent 启动之前、每次模型调用前后，或每次工具调用前后。
我们的 Agent 并不总是需要看到每次工具调用或人类消息返回的 所有 数据，尤其是在数据量很大的情况下。
例如，每次 pull_market_report 工具调用都会返回一份完整的数据导出（数千行）；然而，Agent 只需要其中的几个数字，因此可以限制模型只看到这些行。
过大的用户/人类消息，例如粘贴的通话记录，也会以更高的阈值（50,000 个 token）得到同样的处理，并被保存到 /conversation_history/。
尽管我们尽力卸载冗长的工具调用，但在长时间运行中，上下文仍会逐渐堆积（例如五家公司的搜索、笔记和草稿）。摘要可用于将我们 Agent 的整个上下文窗口浓缩为对目前为止所发生情况的总结，使其能够继续进行研究任务。
SummarizationMiddleware 在每次模型调用之前检查 token 使用量：
你也可以在主题变化时进行摘要 ，而不仅仅是在某个 token 阈值时。自定义摘要提示词可能会有所帮助。
假设你的销售团队有一套固定的季度业务回顾格式。智能体每季度只需要这些指令一次，所以把它们放在系统提示里意味着每次调用都要为它们付费（消耗 token 和响应时间）。相反，你可以把这些信息打包成一个 skill。
skill 是一个指令文件夹（可选包含脚本和参考文档），为智能体提供完成某项专门任务所需的内容。
智能体一开始只看到一段简短描述，只有当 QBR 出现时才加载 qbr-report 的完整指令（其他任务永远不会携带它们）。
Skill 分层加载上下文，因此窗口会一直保持很小，直到某些内容真正相关时才加载。这被称为渐进式披露：模型一开始只看到一份“菜单”，在需要时才拉取完整配方，因此十个 skill 消耗的上下文大约相当于十条单行说明。
完整指令只有在模型判断某个 skill 相关时才会进入上下文（并通过 read_file 工具读取它），因此我们的智能体在没有模板的情况下进行研究，只在需要格式化 QBR 时才加载它。
卸载能有效应对过大的结果，但对于你 已知 会很嘈杂的工作（比如通过数十次搜索和页面研究一家公司），子智能体是一个很好的设计选择。子智能体在自己的上下文窗口中完成这些工作，只返回最终结果，这样主智能体永远不会看到“噪音”。
SubAgentMiddleware 允许我们为子智能体自定义系统提示和可用工具。
在我们的场景中，主智能体把每家公司交给 market-researcher 子智能体。

items.excerpt:
900,000-square-foot California facility features an automated, high-density storage and retrieval system that brings products directly to workers.
Walmart last week opened its fifth “next-generation fulfillment center,” a 900,000-square-foot facility in Stockton, California, that it said will expand the retailer’s ability to provide faster shipping and delivery to customers across California and the West Coast.
First announced by Walmart in 2023 , the new facility now brings its employees together with advanced automation, technology, and machine learning to move products faster and more efficiently. That technology enables Walmart to materially improve storage capacity and increase the number of customer orders the facility can fulfill each day compared with a traditional fulfillment center.
More specifically, the facility features an automated, high-density storage and retrieval system that brings products directly to associates, reducing the traditional 12-step fulfillment process to just five steps. The technology reduces repetitive, manual tasks while allowing associates to focus on higher-value work and helping Walmart move orders through the building more efficiently.
Combined with the rest of Walmart’s fulfillment network, these next-generation fulfillment centers will enable the retailer to reach 95% of the U.S. population with next- or two-day shipping. Walmart Fulfillment Services, Walmart’s end-to-end third-party fulfillment service, will also leverage the space to fulfill third-party Marketplace items.
The opening of the California site follows earlier “next-generation fulfillment centers” such as a 1.5 million square-foot facility in Pennsylvania that opened in 2024 and a 2.2 million-square-foot facility in Indianapolis that opened in 2023. And more are on the way, such as a 1.5-million-square foot building planned for rural Georgia , according to plans unveiled earlier this year.

items.excerpt:
Global race to trade semiconductors and data-transmission equipment has been strong enough to offset economic dampeners like higher tariffs and geopolitical conflicts.
Higher tariffs and geopolitical conflicts have been slowing the flow of global trade, but a powerful new trend is now helping to outweigh those forces, as the global race to build infrastructure for artificial intelligence is giving world trade strong momentum, according to a study from DHL.
The report shows that global goods trade grew faster in the first half of 2026 than in any half-year in the past 15 years, apart from the exceptional Covid rebound. A major driver was strong demand for goods used to build AI infrastructure, such as semiconductors and data-transmission equipment. Trade in AI-enabling goods drove 42% of goods trade growth in 2025, and this share rose to 76% during the first quarter of 2026, according to WTO and OECD analysis.
This is one of the key findings of the latest edition of the “DHL Globalization Tracker” —previously known as the "DHL Global Connectedness Tracker"—which was released October 7 by DHL and New York University's Stern School of Business. Based on more than 30 million data points, the report analyzes international flows of trade, capital, information, and people.
“The biggest story in global trade right now is AI - not tariffs,” said John Pearson, CEO DHL Express. “Every AI query ultimately depends on logistics. Chips, networking equipment, and the many other goods behind this technology must be in the right place at the right time. DHL connects the businesses and markets behind these complex supply chains.”
To be sure, the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted important trade routes. But according to DHL, those effects remained concentrated on economies dependent on the Strait. For example, the value of trade fell 37% in Saudi Arabia and 7% in the United Arab Emirates in the first five months of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025.
Likewise, trade policy created a separate headwind. U.S. tariffs reached their highest levels in decades, but their global impact was limited for two reasons. I like how this piece captures both the positives and the negatives of this new development:
Most people already realized the scary part by now. If AI can decompile games and software, then the entire tech industry is about to explode. Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like, and nobody can stop them. Companies can steal from competitors. Your paid game or app can be open-sourced against your will. This isn't exclusive to old video games, we can apply this to any software. [...]
This is also a big win for preservation. Old games can be ported, modified, enhanced, and made much more easily accessible than before. [...[

🤗 Models | 📄 Paper | 📓 Tutorial notebooks | 🌎 Demo
We introduce HiRO-ACEv2 , the newest update to our High Resolution Output Ai2 Climate Emulator (HiRO-ACE) system. HiROv2 can reproduce even extremely rare rain, wind, and pressure events with high accuracy, while the full system can generate global 3 km climate data at about 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD, a high-resolution global atmospheric model that explicitly simulates storms and other small-scale weather.
HiRO-ACE, introduced earlier in 2026 , has two parts: ACE, an AI model that operates at a coarser 100 km resolution, and HiRO, a model that sharpens those coarse outputs into fine 3 km detail. The biggest change in HiRO-ACEv2 is the new downscaling model, HiROv2, which can now 1) predict several high-resolution fields at once instead of just rainfall, so it can capture a much wider range of extreme weather, and 2) has improved skill in predicting extreme events.
Our main focus with HiRO-ACEv2 was to simulate extreme events well. Changes to how we train HiROv2 improved its ability to reproduce the most intense rain, wind, and pressure values. When given coarsened X-SHiELD data, it matches the target simulation's high-resolution statistics to within 3%, even for events so rare they occur only once in a million data points. It also accurately estimates the total energy of tropical cyclones, including storms it never saw during training, and generates hurricanes with realistic eyes and rain bands, though winds and pressure around the eye remain somewhat more lopsided than in X-SHiELD. Additionally, HiROv2 realistically generates strong winds flowing down mountain slopes.
We also trained an updated version of ACE for this system. Over a 10-year simulation, its hurricanes, average climate patterns, and overall distributions of rain, wind, and pressure all line up well with X-SHiELD. That tells us ACE's coarse simulations are a solid foundation for producing long-term high-resolution climate data.
Putting HiROv2 and ACE together, we generated a full year of global 3 km data. Its statistics closely match X-SHiELD's, even though HiRO was working from a simulation ACE ran on its own rather than from real X-SHiELD data. Across a 10-year run, the energy of HiRO-ACEv2's hurricanes is comparable to X-SHiELD's over the same period, and snapshots from that run show a variety of other extreme events that resemble those in X-SHiELD.

items.title: Tessl Verifiers 正式发布，用仓库内纯文本规则检查每次 Agent 代码变更
items.description: Tessl 发布 Verifiers，规则以 JSON 文件形式存放在仓库中，每次代码变更时由 LLM judge 逐条给出 pass 或 fail，可像 lint 或测试一样在本地、pre-commit 或 CI 中使用。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/virsb1x13670yw25mr9fyxqtt
items.excerpt:
Verifiers: enforce your repo's rules on every agent change
Tessl 发布 Verifiers，规则以 JSON 文件形式存放在仓库中，每次代码变更时由 LLM judge 逐条给出 pass 或 fail，可像 lint 或测试一样在本地、pre-commit 或 CI 中使用。
官方详细介绍 Verifiers 的机制、配置与接入方式，读者可据此把它当作 lint 或测试之外的确定性检查接入现有工作流。
Tessl Verifiers 是用纯文本编写的规则，存放在你的仓库中，并在每次代码变更时进行检查。每次运行时，它们都会返回通过或失败，因此你可以像今天使用 lint 或测试一样使用 verifiers：在本地、在 pre-commit 中，或作为 CI 门禁。它们适用于 linter 无法检查的规则，例如“面向用户的错误必须告诉用户下一步该做什么”。
大多数团队已经为他们的 agent 编写了编码标准。也许他们规定了应该使用哪个 helper，或者哪些 API 应该和不应该被调用，当然还有安全最佳实践，比如绝不记录 token。Agent 通常能很好地遵循这些规则，但它们不会每次都捕捉到所有问题。当某条规则被遗漏时，你通常要到代码审查时才会发现，甚至更晚。
Linters 无法帮助处理大多数这类规则，因为它们只能检查确定性规则。AI 代码审查可以捕捉到它们，但审查会查找 PR 中的一般性问题，并不能在每次运行时可靠地检查同一条规则。在 Tessl，我们需要介于两者之间的东西：一种既能理解你的代码，又能保证每次确定性地运行相同规则的检查。
一个 verifier 是你仓库中的一个 JSON 文件。它包含一条指令、适用条件，以及一份是/否规则清单。当你运行 tessl change verify 时，一个 LLM 评判器会读取相关文件，并将每条规则评分为通过或失败。
一个 verifier 适用于哪些文件，以及它有多严格，是在 tessl.json 的 verify 块中设置的。每个组会获得 info 、 warn 或 error 级别。在 CI 中，警告会被报告，但不会使构建失败。错误会以非零状态退出，并可以阻止 PR。由于作用域和严重性位于 verifier 本身之外，你可以在不同设置的团队之间复用一个 verifier。
默认情况下， tessl change verify 只检查当前变更触及的文件。如果你编辑了一个 verifier 或其配置，它会重新检查该 verifier 覆盖的所有内容。要审计整个项目，请使用 --all 运行它，并在 monorepo 中添加 --recursive 。
默认评判器是 openai/gpt-6-luna 。我们也支持新的 Jev 模型，以防你觉得它在速度、成本或准确性方面更合适，它会为每条规则返回一个判定和置信度分数，而不提供书面推理。你可以使用 --model jev 标志在命令行切换模型选择。.
当规则有明确的是/否答案、你能在变更文件中看到证据，并且没有 linter 或测试能可靠地检查它时，verifier 就很合适。如果 linter 能做这件事，就用 linter。
Verifiers 不适合“这可读吗？”这类主观问题。把规则缩小到你可以用清单检查的程度。
把 verifiers 与你已经在使用的其他工具一起思考会很有帮助。规则在 agent 编写代码之前告诉它该做什么。Verifier 在之后检查结果。它们作为一对配合得很好：规则教授模式，verifier 捕捉 agent 没有遵循它的情况。
该插件的 skill 会帮助你的 agent 编写 verifier、设置其作用域并添加 CI 门禁。作用域最终会出现在 tessl.json 中：
大多数团队从 CI 开始。 在 CI 中验证 agent 变更 指南介绍了如何设置拉取请求门禁。你也可以在 pre-commit 钩子中运行验证器，或者让你的 agent 在打开 PR 之前运行它们。我们不会强推任何一种方案。
我们建议从 warn 级别开始，这样你可以看到验证器在真实 PR 上的表现。一旦你信任它，就把它提升到 error 。
验证器与 Tessl Code Review 是分开的，它们配合得很好。如果审查者总是留下同一条评论，那条评论很可能就是验证器的好候选。
我们在自己的代码库中大量使用 Tessl 验证器，发现它们作为检查手段以及引导 agent 编写更好代码方面都有相当大的进步。我们很想听听你的使用体验，所以为什么不在 discord 上告诉我们呢！

Modern distribution centers frequently employ associates who speak a variety of languages. While workforce diversity is a strength, language barriers can create delays, safety risks, training challenges, and unnecessary dependence on a small number of bilingual employees. Technology that bridges language gaps can therefore expand the labor pool while improving workforce effectiveness. Historically, many operations have relied on supervisors or bilingual associates to bridge communication gaps. The problem is that those employees are frequently pulled away from their primary responsibilities to interpret instructions, explain process changes, or translate safety information. In a high-velocity warehouse environment, those interruptions create hidden productivity losses. Recent advances in real-time voice translation technology are changing this dynamic. Solutions such as Relay’s TeamTranslate allow workers to communicate in their preferred language while messages are translated and delivered to others in near real time. items.excerpt:
Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
MIT研究人员团队在Nature发表论文，提出一个机器学习后处理层，通过从历史数据中学习现有预报模型的错误并修正其输出，将两周到六周范围的预报准确率翻倍。该模型在ECMWF的季节间预报竞赛中获第一名，首次在该时间范围内稳定超过气候学平均值，并显著改善洪水、寒潮等极端天气事件的预测；模型开源、低成本、可附加于任意预报模型，肯尼亚气象部门已接洽用于改进季风季预报。
原文介绍了Nature论文的方法与实测结果，读者可了解AI误差修正如何让两周到六周的天气预报首次稳定超过气候平均值。
2021年，在2月遭遇三场严重冬季风暴之后，得克萨斯州经历了该州历史上最严重的能源基础设施故障。这场中断导致至少246人死亡，并造成食物、水、供暖和电力短缺。
如果能源官员有更多时间准备应对风暴，例如向受灾地区调运更多天然气卡车，这场事件造成的损失本可减轻。不幸的是，两周以上的天气预报出了名地不可靠，这使得全球能源运营商、农民和应急响应官员的准备窗口更加紧张。
包括麻省理工学院研究人员在内的一个团队开发出一种新技术，显著提升了超过两周的天气预报能力。研究人员开发了一种机器学习模型，能够学习纠正现有预报模型中的误差，从而改进两到六周时间范围内的输出。将其应用于一个黄金标准预报模型时，该时间范围内的预报准确率提高了一倍，并在一个知名国际预报竞赛中夺得第一。
在 Nature 的一篇新论文 中，研究人员描述了他们的方法，并展示了它如何使预报首次在两到六周内超越气候学平均值。
“这不仅在这个时间范围的时间平均预报上表现更好——这对试图让供需匹配的农民和能源行业人士已经非常有用——而且还改进了对极端天气事件的预测，无论是洪水、寒潮还是其他什么，”共同作者、麻省理工学院研究科学家Judah Cohen说。“预测这两者都非常重要，但极端事件对社会来说可能是其中影响最大的部分。”
与Cohen共同撰写这篇论文的还有第一作者、哈佛学院本科生Hannah Guan；多伦多大学博士后Soukayna Mouatadid；Genevieve Flaspohler SM ’18、PhD ’22；巴西国家纯数学与应用数学研究所副教授Paulo Orenstein；数据公司DTN的Jeremy Berman；欧洲中期天气预报中心的研究人员Jakob Schloer和Joshua Talib；以及微软的研究人员Alex Lu、Haiyu Dong、Jonathan Weyn、Zekun Ni和Lester Mackey。 更长期的预报
20世纪70年代，长期担任麻省理工学院教授的Edward Lorenz提出了混沌理论的概念，用以描述初始天气条件的微小变化如何导致完全不同的结果。
“他提出了这个理论上的两周限制，超过这个限度，我们就无法预测天气，因为系统中的噪声增长得如此之大，以至于压倒了你开始时拥有的任何信号，”Cohen说。“这对该领域产生了强烈影响，可能阻碍了人们探索两周以上的预报。我从未真正完全相信这一点。理论上，大气可以创造出无限多的模式，但它喜欢一遍又一遍地落入这些偏爱的模式。一旦一件事发生，我认为你可以预测接下来会倒下的多米诺骨牌，以及再接下来会倒下的多米诺骨牌。”
如今，最好的天气预报要么来自动力模型——通过数值模拟大气和海洋随时间的演变，要么来自人工智能模型——从历史天气数据中学习并做出预测。AI 模型在短期天气预报上已显示出改进，但在更长时间范围内，它们甚至比动力模型更差。
科恩就职于麻省理工学院土木与环境工程系，专注于提前两到六周的天气预报，即所谓的次季节预报。“这个时间范围被称为‘可预报性荒漠’，因为在短期，你可以利用气候系统和大气的初始条件，而在更长期，你有这些缓慢变化的边界强迫，比如今年冬天大家都在关注的超级厄尔尼诺现象，”科恩说。“次季节范围无法利用其中任何一种。在大多数情况下，次季节范围的预报就像去赌场掷骰子一样。”
科恩将使用机器学习来减少预报模型误差的最初想法归功于他的合著者莱斯特·麦基，两人已合作十多年。
“我们构建了这个包装器——莱斯特称之为后处理，”科恩说。“我们知道 AI 模型有很多误差，所以我们想也许可以量化这些误差并将其消除。”
其他预报系统进行的是更简单的误差校正，而该研究团队的后处理层利用 AI 基于历史数据从预报系统的错误中学习，并调整其预报。在那个时间范围内，预报员使用所谓的概率预报，即给出各种可能性的概率。
为了构建该模型，研究人员使用了 MIT Engaging——由麻省理工学院研究计算与数据办公室托管的超级计算集群，但最终模型运行并不需要超级计算机。
为了检验他们的模型，去年该研究团队向欧洲中期天气预报中心（ECMWF）提交了三个包含其后处理层的模型，ECMWF 被认为是世界上最好的预报中心。每个季节 ECMWF 都会举办模型之间的预报竞赛。
获得第一名的提交方案将 ECMWF 的预报模型与另一个模型相结合，然后在其上应用后处理校正。这种方法最终使原始模型在次季节范围内的预测能力翻倍。该模型首次实现了比依赖气候平均值的改进。
“到目前为止，还没有人能够证明某个模型在这些次季节预报中比长期平均值更好地预测天气，”科恩说。“它们几乎都比长期平均值差——你 literally 抛硬币都能做得更好。人们甚至质疑在这个时间范围内投资模型是否值得。我们的模型持续优于气候平均值。”
“这是比较重要的发现之一，因为它太难实现了，”Cohen 说。“当 ECMWF 开发出他们自己的、非 AI 的模型误差校正时，它在预测极端天气方面反而变得更差。我认为这是因为传统的误差或偏差校正总是试图趋近均值，而极端天气处于概率的边缘。”

Overall traffic deaths are trending downward. NHTSA’s early estimate shows 36,640 people died in traffic crashes in 2025. That represents a 6.7% decrease from the number of fatalities in 2024.
Even with the numbers going down, getting convicted of a DUI is still serious since the driver still has to deal with the consequences of that conviction.
The long-term consequences of a DUI prompt people to ask, “ Does DUI stay on your record ?” Driving record entries can stay for different periods of time depending on different factors. Most states keep a DUI on a driving record for five to ten years, and some keep it longer.
Criminal records for driving under the influence are generally permanent unless expunged, sealed, or pardoned. items.excerpt:
Executive thesis. Supply-chain risk management is moving from signal accumulation to consequence management. More alerts are not an advantage if the enterprise cannot map them to actual products, suppliers, sites, lanes, inventory, customers, or revenue.
Supply chain risk platforms have become capable of collecting external signals about weather, geopolitics, suppliers, cyber events, infrastructure, finance, and other disruption sources. The challenge is that awareness does not equal response. A long queue of alerts can overwhelm the organization unless the system can determine which events intersect with real operational exposure.
A disruption becomes actionable when it can be mapped to suppliers, sites, products, materials, lanes, customers, inventory, revenue, or service commitments. That requires multi-tier relationship data and a clear understanding of dependencies. Without that context, the enterprise may know that an event occurred but still lack a defensible answer to the question: what does this mean for us?
Risk scoring is most effective when it helps allocate scarce attention. As a result, considering probability, exposure, time horizon, substitution options, inventory, capacity, and customer impact rather than relying on event severity alone. The same storm, port closure, or supplier issue can be immaterial to one business flow and critical to another.
Once material risk is identified, the platform should support the response: investigate, validate, assign an owner, evaluate alternatives, obtain approval, execute mitigation, and track closure. Otherwise the risk platform becomes a notification system whose output has to be managed in separate tools. The value lies in shortening the path from detection to controlled action.
Risk management improves when the organization can model alternatives before a disruption occurs. Alternate suppliers, substitute materials, inventory buffers, routes, capacity, and manual fallback can be evaluated and exercised in advance. That turns risk technology from a monitoring layer into part of the operating model for resilience.

items.excerpt:
Walmart ’s multibillion-dollar warehouse automation push is running into packaging problems, robot breakdowns and higher operating costs, according to a recent Wall Street Journal story . The retailer plans to replace shipping boxes that do not fit its automated systems, while some oversized products still require workers to handle them.
Walmart plans to replace boxes it has used for more than two decades with versions that are 1.5 inches shorter. The new boxes must be taped shut, adding work and expense, although Walmart says they will reduce shelf-stocking time at stores.
The transition involves most of Walmart’s roughly 200 U.S. supply chain buildings. Its warehouse operations rely on more than 140,000 workers to unload, sort, store and ship merchandise.
Rob Montgomery, Head of Supply Chain Operations for Walmart U.S., described the transition to the Journal: “We are kind of in this peak complexity.” He also said Walmart is changing its warehouses while keeping them operating, which adds to the difficulty.
Most of Walmart’s supply chain buildings date to the 1980s and ’90s, and about 80% of its automation construction projects are retrofits. Montgomery said Walmart is installing the equipment while keeping warehouses operating, which complicates the transition.
Different products also require different automated systems, often supplied by different companies. Some goods, including large-screen televisions and jumbo bags of dog food, will need manual assistance for the foreseeable future, Montgomery said.
Symbotic, the Massachusetts robotics company in which Walmart owns a 12.6% stake, supplies equipment that moves merchandise and builds pallets for shipment to stores. A company spokesman told the Journal that about 5% of its product-moving robots were undergoing repairs at any given time in recent months, down from under 10% last year.
Monthly electricity bills at Walmart’s automated grocery facilities can reach $800,000 or more during peak heating or cooling months, compared with roughly $250,000 under more manual operations, a person familiar with the situation told the Journal. The engineers needed to run the equipment also cost more than workers doing manual warehouse tasks, the Journal reported.

items.excerpt:
Reducing Qwen training time by 6x on AI Runtime
Databricks 演示通过系统性性能优化，将 Qwen 3.8 27B 在 AI Runtime 上的微调时间从 7 小时 44 分钟降至 1 小时 17 分钟，提速 6 倍。
原文给出从定位瓶颈到融合内核与数据打包的完整优化路径和量化结果，读者可迁移到自己的 LLM 微调任务。
训练或微调一个数十亿参数的基础模型需要大量算力，通常需要数百到数千小时的 GPU 训练。但调优 LLM 的训练性能颇具挑战，而且诸如 GPU 利用率之类的高层指标可能并未反映你实际的利用率。在这篇博文中，我们将展示如何穿透层层抽象，在 AI Runtime 上将最新 Qwen 3.8 27B 模型的微调速度提升 6 倍。通过系统性的性能优化，即便 GPU 利用率已经达到 98%，我们仍将固定数据集的微调时间从 7 小时 44 分钟缩短到 1 小时 17 分钟。
我们将深入剖析这些改进背后的技术，包括如何衡量真正重要的指标、实现细节，以及每项优化所涉及的设计权衡。
我们从使用 transformers 库和 SFT 训练数据集 HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k 的 Qwen 3.8 27B 标准训练循环开始。
我们在完整数据集上对模型进行基线训练耗时 7 小时 44 分钟，训练期间 GPU 显示平均利用率为 98%。结果是 9,396 tok/s 的训练速度。
这个 GPU 利用率看起来很高，但如前所述，这个数字具有误导性。标准 GPU 利用率指标只统计 GPU 在 做任何事情 的时间百分比，因此它并不能告诉我们模型在 GPU 活跃时对其利用得有多好。要理解这一点，我们需要更深入地观察。
一种方法是 torch trace 机制，我们可以像下面这样调整训练循环（同时限制步数以便快速得到结果）：
表 1：CPU - 14.4 秒，1,714,382 次调用。表中包含按总时间排序的顶级操作。

此外，我们在批次中存在过度填充的问题：输入张量必须是矩形的，每一行都会被填充到该批次的最大 token 数。我们将展示一个可用于 LLM 的技巧来尽量减少这种情况。
在接下来的章节中，我们将深入探讨每个技术主题，涵盖它是什么、推荐的最佳实践，以及应用它时需要考虑的关键权衡。
你可能会注意到某些 kernel 出现得非常频繁！特别是对于 Qwen，批量矩阵乘法 kernel 在一个步骤中运行超过 30,000 次。
在本例中，我们将首先探讨融合 kernel。融合 kernel 将多个较小的 GPU kernel 组合成一个单元。这可以通过避免 GPU 的高带宽内存与其更高带宽的片上内存之间代价高昂的传输来帮助提升性能。此外，它还可以实现更高效的 GPU 核心调度。
有了这么多额外的 kernel，虽然 torch.compile 可能可行，但运行起来会花费很长时间。因此，使用手动融合的 kernel 来减少原始算子数量是很好的第一步。此外，像 Flash Attention 这样众所周知的融合并不是 torch.compile 自身能够发现的。
transformers 库默认对标准注意力层使用 torch 的 SDPA 。但事实证明，我们看到的许多小运算来自非标准的门控 delta 网络层。幸运的是，对于这些层，有两个 kernel——causal-conv1d 和 flash-linear-attention——它们被编写用于融合每层中的许多此类运算。我们如何发现这一点？Qwen 的 transformers 库实现 已经告诉我们它支持哪些 kernel：
我们通常推荐第一种，尤其是配合我们的 docker 容器支持 ，在构建时将所有 kernel 安装到容器中，以减少作业启动所需的时间。
虽然 kernelhub 很方便，但由于 kernel 通常明确依赖于所安装的 torch 和 cuda 版本，你的特定配置可能没有可用的 kernel，而 transformers 模型会静默回退到未优化、性能低下的 kernel。

An ETH Zurich scientist has shown that bacteria and digital manufacturing can also be used to build free-form architectural elements.
The process is seen as a promising, less energy-intensive alternative to cement. Previously, it has primarily been used to stabilise soils, moulded tiles, and in research.
The research suggests that living bacteria can bond sand and other loose grains together into a solid material by forming calcium carbonate, the mineral that makes up limestone.
The process looks in part like 3D printing (see video below).
Cement manufacturing is one of the largest sources of CO2 emissions in the construction industry. At the Department of Architecture, Karen Antorveza Paez , who has just completed her doctorate at ETH Zurich, is researching an alternative that works in a totally different way: instead of firing rocks at over 1,000°C, she is getting bacteria to bond grains of sand together into solid architectural elements.
“We’re using bacteria to produce a sort of mineral glue,” explains Antorveza Paez.
When certain types of bacteria are combined with sand or other solid grains, they join the particles together into a solid structure made of interlocking, microscopic calcite crystals.
The process is called microbiologically induced calcite precipitation (MICP), or simply biocementation. It’s nothing new: the bacteria used for this, Sporosarcina pasteurii, have been under research for many years, such as for stabilising loose subsoil.
They have also been used in concrete research for “self-healing” concrete, where the introduction of bacterial spores causes cracks to seal over on their own.
Antorveza Paez’s innovation is how the process is controlled: not as an addition to existing building materials, but as an architectural material in its own right. To achieve this, she combined two research fields that had until then been largely separate: biocementation and digital manufacturing.
While it has long been known that bacteria can bond sand together into solid objects under certain conditions, Antorveza Paez explains that, “What was missing were manufacturing processes whereby these biological processes can be controlled as required and used to make architectural elements”.
In the course of writing her doctoral thesis, three scientific studies were conducted that describe two different manufacturing methods.

Neura Robotics has launched Neuron AI, its multimodal foundation model for physical AI.
Combining 3D vision, touch, audio, robot state and language with memory, Neuron AI enables robots to act on information beyond what cameras alone can capture, as well as retain relevant context when objects disappear from view.
Its “Perception-Language-Action” (PLA) architecture connects what a robot sees, hears and feels with what it has already done, turning multisensory information into physical action.
David Reger, founder and CEO of Neura Robotics, says: “An intelligent robot needs a brain that brings its senses together and remembers what happened.
“With Neuron AI, we are building the brain of the physical world: Physical AI that turns human expertise and physical experience into capabilities robots can learn and apply. Developed in Germany, built for the world.”
Cameras capture geometry, color and position, but provide no information about contact, force or sound. Humans also rely on more than sight: they feel whether a screw has caught and hear when a connector clicks into place.
Neuron AI applies this principle to robots. Rather than treating each sensor as a separate input, the model encodes 3D vision, tactile and force data, audio, robot state and language, aligns them in one shared space over time, and turns them into a single stream of action.
Multisensory perception matters most for tasks that cameras cannot solve on their own. When a robot opens a lock, only sound and touch confirm that it is really open. With touch, a robot can grasp objects it cannot see.
The additional senses also improve tasks that vision can already handle: in welding, for example, the quality of a seam can be judged from the sound of the process.
In addition, Neuron AI has a memory function. To act in the physical world, a robot needs a sense of cause and effect and object permanence, the ability to remember objects when they are out of sight, which humans acquire in their first two years of life.
Unlike purely digital AI, a robot acts in a continuous physical world and must keep track of objects and the consequences of its own actions over time, often without seeing them.
Neura adapted the model’s architecture specifically to introduce memory and trains it on dedicated datasets that make use of it.

items.description: OpenAI Core Experimentation 团队工程师分享用 GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 在 Codex 中做代码维护的实践，团队已合并超过 1,400 个维护 PR，删除逾 80 万行代码。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/wn2lwzshkg8gt2sbjuj1qxd8y
items.excerpt:
Maintaining software with the GPT-6 family
OpenAI Core Experimentation 团队工程师分享用 GPT-6 Astra 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 在 Codex 中做代码维护的实践，团队已合并超过 1,400 个维护 PR，删除逾 80 万行代码。
作者以一手实践给出可直接复用的 Codex 提示词和模型成本对比，读者可按小任务起步迁移到自己的代码库维护。
每个不断增长的代码库都需要维护：删除未使用的代码、清理已完成的实验、修复测试。在 OpenAI，编码智能体帮助我们更快地构建，这也增加了我们的维护需求。
我在 OpenAI 的核心实验团队工作，我们负责构建和维护支持公司各项实验的软件，从前端更新到模型服务效率的改进。
GPT-6 Astra 的发布帮助我们更快地构建和维护软件，而 GPT-6.1 Sol 以更低的成本交付了类似的结果。在这篇文章中，我将分享我们如何使用这些模型来发现清理机会、收集证据，并准备变更以供审查。
在智能体编码出现之前，许多软件工程团队依赖与运行时日志集成的复杂静态分析系统来检测和删除未使用的代码。即使有这些系统和细致的代码审查，错误仍会发生。我记得有几次因误删代码而导致的事故。需要考虑的边缘情况太多了，比如反射会干扰静态分析，或者某条未使用的代码路径可能被启用以缓解未来的事故。
借助 Codex 中的 GPT-5.6 Sol，我可以指定一个要调查的区域和明确的验证标准，然后让模型编写静态分析并删除死代码。这些有针对性的提示比我们现有的静态分析系统更容易开发和维护，可靠性也相当。
当我们获得 GPT-6 Astra 的访问权限时，我们想看看它能否处理更宽泛的请求，自行判断该从哪里入手、需要哪些证据来为每一次删除提供依据。我们一开始用了一段简短的 Codex 提示，它对 GPT-5.6 Sol 来说过于模糊，无法完全处理。就是下面这段，连拼写错误都保留着：
Astra 很好地处理了这种模糊性。它查看了过去的 PR，从 Slack 讨论串中收集上下文，并检查了内部项目跟踪器。它阅读了生产性能分析表，以确认被删除的代码行从未被执行到。Astra 还解释了每次删除的理由，这加快了我们的审查速度。
看到 Astra 表现如此出色后，五名工程师协作在多个代码库中运行该提示的变体，我们合并了 1400 多个拉取请求，删除了超过 80 万行代码。我们主要是在从事其他项目的同时，利用两周的业余时间完成了大部分工作。代码审查被分派给各个团队，并附上每个受影响项目的相关背景。这些删除带来了可衡量的收益。例如，一个服务的容器镜像从 3.31GB 缩小到 1.72GB，减少了 48%；另一组清理从我们的测试套件中移除了约 400 个视觉快照变体。
软件维护中一个更难的问题是清理 过期 实验。这些实验未必未被使用：它们的代码可能仍在生产环境中运行，或者依赖于随时可能变化的资格评估，这使得静态分析困难得多。过去，我们团队通过确定性静态分析并辅以数据库查询来清理过期实验，并使用我们最强大的模型（当时是 GPT-5.6 Sol）来构建和改进相关脚本。我们知道这导致了许多假阴性，即我们的分析无法识别出真正过期的实验。
鉴于我们使用 GPT-6 Astra 清理死代码取得了成功，我决定再试一个简短的提示词来清理过期的实验。我不确定该如何开始，于是和 Astra 一起头脑风暴，并让它写一个简短的提示词，以便在新线程中尝试：
Astra 遵循了提示词中的安全防护措施，并准备了带有证据的更改，供我们团队审查。我对它的拉取请求发表了评论，然后让 Astra 查看我的评论、采纳我的反馈，并制定一个新提示词来扫描我们的整个代码库。我担心要清理的东西太多，无法确定优先级，所以我也让 Astra 帮我处理这个问题。Astra 建议使用这个提示词：
生成的报告很有前景。利用我们的埋点数据，Astra 调查了每个过期实验的 CPU 成本，排名前几的结果都是巨大的效率收益，而这些实验多年来一直没有人将其标记为过期。我仔细验证了那些较大的结果，并继续进行了全面清理，移除了数百个实验和功能开关。
有一个例子体现了 Astra 的判断力：几年前，我们的一位工程师创建了一个 Statsig 功能开关，允许内部开发者覆盖我们所有其他与新功能相关的功能开关，用于测试目的。这个配置通过一行 Python 代码实现，将该开关映射到所有其他功能。那一行代码与数百个类似的功能开关映射放在一起，看起来毫不起眼。
Astra 发现上面那一行代码导致了显著的 CPU 扇出，因为它将该开关映射到了 所有 功能。它调查了 CPU 成本，但将这一发现提交人工审查，因为该开关在我们的功能开关管理控制台中被明确标记为“Permanent”（永久），并且可能仍具有运维用途。经过审查，我们移除了该开关，预计在主要受影响的服务中节省了 0.42% 的 CPU。

items.title: ALAN Announces 2026 Humanitarian Logistics Awards Winners
items.description: The winners have "truly inspired us by repeatedly stepping up to help – all without asking what’s in it for them," said Kathy Fulton of ALAN.
items.excerpt:
Last week, the American Logistics Aid Network (ALAN) today announced the winners of its 2026 Humanitarian Logistics Awards.
“We recognize a group of outstanding organizations and individuals who exemplify what selfless logistics is all about,” said ALAN Executive Director Kathy Fulton in a statement. “They have truly inspired us by repeatedly stepping up to help – all without asking what’s in it for them.”
Paul Delp -- ALAN’s Lifetime Achievement Award
Paul Delp received his award for his body of philanthropic work both personally and as president of Lansdale Warehouse. This work included providing Mitzvah Circle with the cost-free loan of a forklift for a year (a contribution that made it possible for the nonprofit to serve more than 500,000 people during 2025) and making a Lansdale warehouse available as a donation collection center for survivors of the September 11 attacks. It also included Paul’s service as a board member for the Red Cross Board of Montgomery County.
Lynden Air Cargo -- ALAN’s Outstanding Contribution to Disaster Relief Efforts Award
Lynden Air Cargo was honored for donating 61,563 pounds of air cargo capacity to support Bethel Search and Rescue’s relief efforts in Western Alaska following last October’s Typhoon Halong – and for working closely with organizations such as GCI, the Alaska Foundation of Natives, Team Rubicon, and other local Alaska air cargo carriers to assist with donation collection, staging and distribution for typhoon survivors.
Niagara Cares --ALAN’s Outstanding Contribution to Disaster Relief Efforts Award
Niagara Cares received its honor for donating and rapidly distributing more than 220,000 gallons of clean drinking water to the survivors of the 2025 floods in Central Texas’s Kerrville region – and for the financial donation it made to support long-term recovery and rebuilding efforts.
UPS -- ALAN’s Outstanding Contribution To Disaster Relief Efforts Award
UPS received its award for the ongoing work of its UPS Foundation. In 2025, UPS and The UPS Foundation delivered hope when it mattered most by contributing more than $16 million in grants and logistics support. This support helped humanitarian organizations respond to 80 disasters and crises around the globe, providing relief to more than 1.7 million survivors.

items.title: Google DeepMind and Singapore Government collaborate to build fine-tuned AI model for scam detection
items.description: Learn how Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore uses lightweight on-device Gemma models to intercept conversational scams in private chats with zero cloud data egress.
items.excerpt:
Collaborating with the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech Singapore) to protect users without compromising privacy.
Scams, such as investment fraud, fake job offers, and impersonation of public officials make up over half of Singapore’s reported crimes, and account for more than S$4 billion in losses since 2019 . At the same time, scam tactics have shifted from simple phishing to complex social engineering, whereby attackers manipulate victims with convincing conversations before requesting money. Such scams now account for up to 80% of all losses.
To address this, Google DeepMind and the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech Singapore) have been working together as part of our National AI Partnership with the Singapore Government. Together, we've fine-tuned a privacy-preserving, on-device scam detection model.
Generic models often struggle with local deception techniques, making scam detection harder. To address this, Google’s lightweight Gemma model was fine-tuned on local scam conversations. These ranged from impersonations of public institutions, banks, and local figures, to trending regional schemes. This ensures the fine-tuned model will be able to distinguish benign social chatter from genuine manipulation when deployed in applications installed by citizens.
Unlike traditional threat detection, which relies on server-side scanning of messages in the cloud, this model can process conversation data directly on-device. When integrated into applications, this will allow faster analysis of conversation patterns to detect manipulative intent and help citizens act before financial or credential exposure can occur.
The roll out of the model within applications will be carefully phased and developed in partnership with the Singapore Government. When deployed, the model will only be able to access on-device conversations with the user's consent, in accordance with the terms of use of that application. As the model runs entirely on-device, neither the Singapore Government nor Google, will be able to access users’ conversations through its deployment.
Fighting scams shouldn't mean sacrificing personal privacy. Working with Google DeepMind, we're bringing advanced AI protection directly onto citizens' devices. This allows us to catch highly targeted, local scam attempts in real time while keeping personal communications private.
